name: Wyoming Interstate Kanda Lateral
researcher_notes: The Kanda Lateral is a separate new 24-inch supply line, built under Federal Energy Regulatory Commission docket CP07-14, and it has no row of its own. The existing Wyoming Interstate row (P0282) is the whole system, so this is a new expansion-style row under that system name. Wyoming Interstate Company filed the application on October 23, 2006 for about 123 miles of 24-inch pipe in Uintah and Daggett Counties, Utah, carrying up to 406,000 dekatherms a day (Federal Register notice of November 9, 2006). A Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration special-permit notice of March 3, 2011 gives 123.9 miles of 24-inch line, starting in Uintah County, Utah, running north into southwestern Wyoming and ending in Sweetwater County, Wyoming, in service in 2007. The Energy Information Administration August 2026 release lists it as two completed phases (sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel rows 473 and 481, 51.5 and 71.5 miles, 24 inch, completed December 2007); that release is one origin and was checked with the verifier by project name only in the workbook, so it supports status and start year as a second source of the same history. Length is staged as 123.9 miles from the 2011 notice; the 2006 notice says about 123. Capacity is 406,000 Dth/d from the 2006 notice and is not converted. Status operating is supported by the 2011 notice and by the 2022 Federal Register notice that refers to the existing Kanda Lateral. The $143 million cost in the 2006 notice covers the lateral plus a compressor expansion, so no cost is staged. Owner not staged: no checked source names the owner. The existing P0282 row lists Kinder Morgan (parent Kinder Morgan Inc), which is the likely owner to adopt after one check. Start and end town names and the route were not found; the lateral starts near the Questar Kanda compressor complex area in Uintah County, but that is not confirmed by a verified source, so StartLocation and EndLocation are blank. No route was researched. Confidence high for existence, length, diameter and status; capacity is a filing-time design figure.
